claim: Adaptive n-back or WM training reliably improves the trained task and close WM tasks (near transfer): n-back g=0.62, other WM g=0.24 (Soveri); near transfer 0.44-0.46 (Sala and Gobet).
agent_test: Not testable as such; our agent has no trained weights. Skip.
audit_note: Soveri's n-back g=0.62 is transfer to untrained n-back tasks, and its WM g=0.24 falls to 0.18 after control analysis, so 'reliably' is generous for other WM tasks; numbers match.

claim: Far transfer to fluid intelligence is small and shrinks toward zero with active controls: Gf g=0.16 (Soveri), 0.11 after control analysis, 0.11 [-0.02,0.24] (Sala and Gobet), nonverbal 0.05 treated vs 0.20 untreated (Melby-Lervag 2016).
agent_test: Control arm only: a repeated-task warm-up stage vs plain prompt at equal tokens on a held-out reasoning set; expect no gain.
audit_note: Sala and Gobet Gf 0.11 [-0.02,0.24] is pooled over control types, not an active-only estimate; numbers all match.

claim: The Jaeggi 2008 effect (trained d=0.65 vs control d=0.25, F(1,67)=5.27) rests on small passive-control cells (trained subgroups n=7 to 11) and one Gf test per dose level.
agent_test: Evaluation hygiene: judge scaffold gains with several test items and a matched equal-token control, not small cells with one test.
audit_note: Jaeggi PMC2383308 listed in a01/a02 is the wrong PMCID (a Canadian Family Physician page); PMC2383929 is correct. Per-subgroup n=7-11 comes from Redick 2013 and could not be opened in full, but is consistent with Jaeggi's totals; RAPM was used at 8 days and BOMAT at 12, 17 and 19 days.

claim: Part of the reported Gf gain is expectation: a placebo-only manipulation produced RAPM d=0.50 (N=50), and Gf effects fall when the comparison group is active.
agent_test: Compare the scaffold against an equal-length placebo scaffold with no content, not only against a bare prompt.

claim: Moderator results disagree: Soveri finds active vs passive control g difference 0.03 (p=.429), while Sala and Gobet (passive 0.18 vs active 0.05) and Melby-Lervag 2016 (untreated 0.20 vs treated 0.05) find a gap. Gap search: the gap is real for nonverbal ability in Melby-Lervag 2016 (Q(1)=6.09, p=.01) and not for verbal, decoding or arithmetic; Soveri's null may reflect different inclusion rules.
agent_test: Not agent-testable; sets how much weight to give a passive-baseline gain.

claim: Several replications found no transfer of dual n-back training to Gf: Redick 2013 (75 completers, power >.99 for medium effects, with active and no-contact controls), Thompson 2013 (about 58, passive and active controls), Chooi and Thompson 2012 (93, small cells) and Sprenger 2013 (253 across two experiments). In the Pahor 2022 data the retrospective sample (no-contact control) gave B=0.23, p=.022 on Matrix Reasoning while the replication sample (active general-knowledge control) gave B=0.07, p=.50.
agent_test: None; confirms there is no training shortcut.
audit_note: Pahor 2022 replication sample used an active control (general-knowledge training), not a passive control, and Pahor is Jaeggi's own group; 'well-powered' fits Redick (power >.99) but not Chooi and Thompson (cells n=4-21, n~58).
claim_before_audit: Well-powered replications failed to reproduce the Jaeggi effect on Gf: Redick 2013 (n=75 completers, power >.99 for medium effect), Thompson 2013 (n about 58), Chooi and Thompson 2012 (n=93), Sprenger 2013 (N=253). Pahor 2022 replication sample (passive control): B=0.07, p=.50 versus B=0.23, p=.022 in the retrospective sample.

claim: Trained-task gain and reasoning gain decouple: in Richey 2014 spatial complex WM rose d=3.16 while visual analogy moved d=0.05; WM change vs analogy change r<=.17.
agent_test: Test whether an agent that improves on an n-back style retrieval probe also improves matrix-style reasoning; expect decoupling.

claim: Whatever far transfer exists is not durable: nonverbal ability at about 5 months follow-up g=-0.05 [-0.21,0.11] (k=12, Melby-Lervag 2016).
agent_test: None.

claim: Across ten first-order meta-analyses (WM, video games, music, chess, exergames) uncorrected far transfer has grand mean g=0.12 and falls to g=0.00 with active controls only, true heterogeneity zero (Gobet and Sala 2022, data from Sala et al. 2019); the authors also produced the data, so not independent labs.
agent_test: Use as a prior: any claimed LLM gain from a practice stage needs an equal-token control before it is believed.

claim: No study was found that trains an LLM on working-memory tasks to raise reasoning; the LLM literature probes WM and does not train it (absence from a limited search).
agent_test: Possible experiment: fine-tune on n-back, then test on ARC-style items. Out of scope for a scaffold-only agent.

claim: Instruction-tuned LLMs show a steep, size-dependent n-back drop: Llama 3.1 8B retrieval 1.00/0.14/0.17 at 1/2/3-back, Llama 3.1 70B 1.00/0.99/0.93, GPT-3.5 1.00/0.51/0.43.
agent_test: Put agent memory in an explicit external buffer and compare n-back-like retrieval with and without it at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Whether non-GPT-4 models are capacity-limited at n-back is contested: Gong 2024 finds no model but GPT-4 above d'=1, while Hu and Lewis attribute failure to task understanding and show Llama 70B at 75% retrieval at 8-back and gains from in-context curriculum. Gap 4: the two papers differ in prompt (m/- labels vs retrieved letter plus a 24-letter demo), metric (d' vs retrieval accuracy and log-probabilities) and models; no one-model equal-token test exists.
agent_test: Raw n-back prompt vs decomposed retrieve-then-compare prompt on the same model at equal tokens.

claim: Externalised steps lift LLM performance on WM-bound tasks: Math Magic 0-26% without CoT vs 96.7% (o3-mini) with; rehearsal prompt +18 points on Object Counting; CoT theory shows serial problems become solvable.
agent_test: Scratchpad with rehearsal vs same tokens of unstructured thinking on tracking tasks.
audit_note: o3-mini (96.7%) is a reasoning model rather than a CoT-prompted one, and Huang 2025 calls it ISR on the Mathematical Mentalism task; wording slightly loose, numbers match (rehearsal 94.8%, +18).

claim: LLMs do not hold hidden state like humans: GPT-4o gave Yes-probability sum 1.085 on Number Guessing (ideal 1.0) and failed 173 of 200 Yes-No Deduction trials; seven models scored 0.
agent_test: Force the agent to write the hidden choice into a visible note and measure the Yes-No failure rate.

claim: Proactive interference limits LLM retrieval: llama4-maverick near 100% at 2 tracked keys, below 5% at 46; telling the model to forget changes under 10 points.
agent_test: Mock-QA reset or memory pruning vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Long context is not usable working memory: only about half of 17 long-context models keep satisfactory RULER performance at 32K tokens, and interference grows with updates.
agent_test: Full-context vs summarised-memory arms at a fixed token budget.
audit_note: RULER says only about half of 17 models keep satisfactory performance at 32K; the 'long context is not usable working memory' framing is interpretive but Wang and Sun do show log-linear accuracy decline with interference.

claim: RL on verifiable game or procedural tasks transfers to reasoning in LLMs (ViGaL math avg 47.7 to 50.6; SPIRAL Qwen3-4B 34.0 to 44.5; Reasoning Gym Algebra +29.1) but unevenly (ARC no gain; SPIRAL vs fixed opponent 29.6 below base 34.0). This is training, the nearest LLM analogue of Jaeggi. Controls: ViGaL random-label RL 49.4 vs base 49.1 (no gain) and SFT on the same Snake data 47.2 (below base); SPIRAL gain shrinks for tuned models (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct +2.0, DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-7B +1.4). No ARC test in either paper.
agent_test: Out of scope for a scaffold-only agent; serves as an upper-bound contrast to the human null.

claim: Transfer theories (PRIMs) predict transfer only through shared task components, matching the near-transfer-only human pattern.
agent_test: None.

claim: Larger pooled evidence after 2017 agrees: Sala and Gobet 2020 (m=41, k=393, N=2,375 children) far-transfer g=0.001 with active controls; near transfer g=0.468 for nearest tasks; no true heterogeneity. No large multi-site WM-training RCT after 2017 reverses the null (absence from a limited search).
agent_test: None; confirms no training shortcut.
audit_note: Sala and Gobet 2020, Gobet and Sala 2022 and the earlier Sala and Gobet 2017 are the same two authors, so 'larger pooled evidence agrees' is one lab; Blacker 2017 is a single N=73 study, not a multi-site RCT; numbers (m=41, k=393, N=2,375, g=0.001, 0.468) are correct.

claim: The n-back training effect on Matrix Reasoning, where present, runs through near transfer to untrained n-back (indirect effect 0.19 [0.09,0.31], three RCTs, N=460), and the total effect fails to replicate (B=0.07, p=.50) in the passive-control replication sample.
agent_test: If a probe task shares structure with the target task, gains on it may predict gains on the target; test with an n-back-like probe and matched matrix items.

claim: Length-matched placebo prompts recover most of a prompt scaffold's gain on small code models (placebo +19.5 vs structured +22.0 points best-of-8; placebo trails full skill by 2.4, p=0.60) while a frontier model sits at ceiling (95.1% to 96.9%, none significant). Blind resampling at equal budget matches content-bearing feedback pooled (26 vs 26 unlocks).
agent_test: Every scaffold gain claim needs three controls: equal-length placebo scaffold, labels-only scaffold, and blind resampling at equal output budget.

claim: An equal-token control is not neutral for LLMs: irrelevant padding drops accuracy from 0.92 to 0.68 at 3,000 tokens, while meaningless filler tokens can add real compute after dense supervision.
agent_test: Report both neutral-text padding and content-free scaffold controls and say which was used.
audit_note: Levy 0.92 to 0.68 is an average over models at about 3,000 tokens; Pfau filler gains are shown in small 34M transformers on synthetic tasks with dense supervision, so the 'for LLMs' generalisation is mild.

claim: Low-baseline people gain more on trained tasks in cognitive training (pooled correlation magnitude 0.449, 82 coefficients from 25 papers, I2=91%), but evidence is inconclusive and about trained-task gain, not far transfer; training mostly moves efficiency (strategy, routine), not capacity.
agent_test: Scale scaffold strength to the model's baseline on the item class; test whether gains shrink for stronger models (as in SPIRAL: +10.5 on Qwen3-4B-Base vs +1.4 on DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-7B).

claim: No study yet tests an external scratchpad or memory buffer against equal tokens of free chain of thought on n-back or tracking; written-after reasoning did not lift ChatGPT's n-back capacity (about 3).
agent_test: Run the three-arm probe: explicit state record, free reasoning with equal tokens, no reasoning.
